findings.passage: I have seen first hand the long term affects of gun violence, not only the physical scars, but also the invisible ones from their trauma. It is an epidemic everywhere, including in Missouri. In my first term, I worked to remove the physician gag order for gun safety education. As a Mom’s Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate I promise to continually work for common sense gun laws in Missouri.
findings.note: Campaign issues page, Gun Safety section. Calls gun violence an epidemic, says he worked in his first term to remove the limit on doctors giving gun safety education, and promises to keep working for common sense gun laws. Page is undated; year is approximate.
subjects: physician gag order on gun safety talk

findings.passage: Well, the Second Amendment talks about a well-regulated militia first off and the right of people to keep and bear arms shall not be infringed. We do have really, really lax gun laws here. I am a gun-sense candidate. I believe that we do need to have more regulations, make sure that we get illegal guns off the street, and to make sure that individuals who have firearms are storing them properly.
findings.note: Answer in a 2024 candidate interview published by a local TV news site (ABC17). Says Missouri gun laws are lax and he wants more regulation, illegal guns removed, and proper storage. Interview date not shown in the fetched text; year only.

findings.passage: Sure. I mean, obviously a background check, you know, at all levels. And then making sure that there might be a need for insurance as well. I mean, I have a vehicle, I have to have insurance. That's something that's definitely on the table, making sure that there is, you know, adequate training that we are storing firearms safely.
findings.note: Same ABC17 interview, asked what ideal gun legislation looks like. Names background checks at all levels, possible gun insurance, training and safe storage.

findings.passage: I live with someone who actually had their lives saved by some of these red flag laws where, you know, people that had been diagnosed with mental illness or that sort of thing don't have access to firearms because of the volatility of who that person is. And so this is something I take really personally.
findings.note: Same ABC17 interview. Speaks of red flag laws having helped someone close to him, in the context of limiting gun access for people with serious mental illness.
subjects: limits on who may have a gun
